candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Reduction of Risk Potential: implement interventions based on identified aspiration risk, monitor response to treatment plans, and recognize changes requiring reassessment.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — individualized aspiration precautions for post-stroke dysphagia
candidate.educational_objective: Implement post-stroke dysphagia precautions according to the individualized swallowing evaluation—using appropriate positioning, texture/viscosity, pacing, cueing, and supervision—and continue monitoring because modified diets do not eliminate aspiration risk.

options.A: Follow the individualized swallowing plan for posture/positioning, food texture and liquid consistency, pacing, cueing, and supervision during oral intake, and reassess if swallowing status changes.
options.B: Use the same thickened-liquid level and chin-tuck position for every client with post-stroke dysphagia regardless of the swallowing evaluation.
options.C: Encourage rapid eating so the meal is completed before fatigue develops, even if the client coughs or requires repeated swallows.
options.D: Assume texture modification eliminates aspiration risk, so ongoing observation and reassessment are unnecessary once the diet order is written.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. ASHA guidance emphasizes individualized dysphagia management based on swallowing assessment, including posture/positioning, compensatory strategies, bolus or diet-texture modification, pacing/cueing, and patient/caregiver education. Texture-modified foods and thickened liquids do not eliminate aspiration or pneumonia risk, and reassessment may be needed when clinical status changes. B applies one strategy to every patient even though postural and consistency recommendations depend on swallowing physiology. C may increase risk when fatigue, impulsivity, coughing, or multiple swallows are present. D incorrectly treats diet modification as a guarantee of airway protection.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For a stroke patient with confirmed dysphagia who is permitted oral intake, aspiration-risk reduction requires individualized swallowing strategies and diet/positioning recommendations with ongoing monitoring; no single posture or consistency is appropriate for all patients and modification does not eliminate aspiration risk.

candidate.source_locator: ASHA Adult Dysphagia — intervention may include compensatory swallowing strategies, posture considerations, bolus consistency modification, pacing/cueing, education, and reassessment; Diet Texture Modifications: texture/thickened-liquid changes must be individualized and may not eliminate aspiration or pneumonia risk.
